text:
Marathon Petroleum shares fell 1.3% today, continuing a steep two-week slide of 7.3%. The main driver is crude oil prices — US oil dropped to $103.37 per barrel today on reports of potential Iran peace talks, and refiners like Marathon are caught between lower crude costs (which help margins initially) and the uncertainty that softer oil demand signals. The stock's weakness accelerated after the company announced a leadership change and company update on October 29th, which coincided with analyst warnings that Big Oil earnings guidance—not just current results—may disappoint investors going forward.

The refining backdrop adds complexity: US refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with adequate fuel inventories, so there's no supply crunch to support prices or margins. Any dip in crude prices or demand signals translates directly to refiner margin pressure, making the diplomatic chatter around Iran tensions particularly relevant for a company whose earnings depend on the spread between crude input costs and refined product sales.
